content.text:
## Bottom line

**The preferred cave tour is not supported for nine adults together on Friday, November 6 under Schramsberg’s published rules.** Nine is a large party: parties of seven or more must use a private tour and cannot join a public tour. Private tours are published as **Sunday–Thursday mornings only**, excluding Friday. A Friday visit would therefore depend on an explicitly confirmed exception—not something the public evidence promises. Splitting the party must not be assumed permissible. ([Winery experiences](https://www.schramsberg.com/visit-schramsberg/), [official FAQ](https://www.schramsberg.com/faq/))

The year was not specified; **November 6, 2026 is a Friday**. The comparison below applies the published November season and Friday restrictions, not confirmed availability.

## Experiences and published reference prices

| Experience | What is actually offered | Published reference price | Fit for nine on Friday |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cave Tour with Classic Tasting** | Indoor cave tour and six wines, including Schramsberg sparkling and Davies Vineyards wines; public tours may combine groups. | **$100/person** | **Not supported:** public parties are limited to six; nine must use the private route. |
| **Cave Tour with Reserve Wine & Cheese Pairing** | Indoor cave tour, six wines, artisan cheeses, meat, fruits and nuts. | **$150/person; $75/non-drinker** | **Not supported as a public tour for nine.** A private version is subject to the private-tour restrictions. |
| **Private Tour & Tasting** | Classic or Reserve options above, or **Custom Tasting**, selecting six wines from available Schramsberg/Davies inventory. | Custom: **$120/person**; selected experience determines private-tour cost and minimum/maximum party requirements. | Nine falls within the FAQ’s **up-to-12** private-party ceiling, but experience-specific limits still apply. **Sunday–Thursday mornings only, subject to availability—not Friday.** |
| **Classic — Tasting Only** | Six wines; approximately one hour. In **November–April**, standing in the historic caves. **This is not a cave tour.** | **$70/person** | **Unsuitable for nine together:** maximum six in the November cave setting. |
| **Custom — Tasting Only** | Six wines chosen from available inventory; approximately one hour; same seasonal setting and limits. | **$80/person** | **Unsuitable for nine together:** maximum six in November. |

Experience descriptions, seasonal limits and prices come from the [current winery-experiences page](https://www.schramsberg.com/visit-schramsberg/); the large-party/public-tour rules and private ceiling come from the [FAQ](https://www.schramsberg.com/faq/). The May–October outdoor tasting-only limit is four, but that does **not** govern this November visit.

These are **published reference prices, not a nine-person quote or evidence of an available appointment**. Private experience minimums and maximums are not fully specified publicly. Published club pricing also exists, but the page limits the reduced-price benefit to two reservations per account; it should not be extended to all nine without confirmation.

## Non-drinkers and conflicting official information

- **Non-drinkers do not attend free.** The FAQ requires a per-person fee regardless of tasting participation and says non-alcoholic beverages are available. The Reserve experience specifically lists **$75 for non-drinkers**. No separate non-drinker price is published on the experience page for Classic or Custom; do not assume a discount. All visitors must be **21 or older**, so “nine adults” alone does not establish eligibility. ([Non-drinker policy](https://www.schramsberg.com/simple-faqs/i-am-pregnantdesignated-driver-etc-and-i-will-not-be-tasting-may-i-tour-for-free/), [experiences](https://www.schramsberg.com/visit-schramsberg/))
- The official FAQ contains conflicting material: it lists a **$65 public tour** and says tasting-only visits are unavailable, whereas the dedicated experiences page explicitly offers tasting-only appointments and lists the prices above. **Use the dedicated experience listings as the stronger reference for products and prices**, while recognizing that the inconsistency needs clarification. ([FAQ](https://www.schramsberg.com/faq/))
- “Splitting a tasting” is also described inconsistently: the experiences page prohibits it, while the FAQ allows sharing but still charges each guest the standard fee. **Neither statement authorizes dividing a nine-person party into separate bookings.**

## Most useful unresolved questions

1. Is **2026** the intended year, and are all nine guests at least 21?
2. Is Friday fixed, or could a **Sunday–Thursday morning** private cave tour be considered?
3. Would Schramsberg explicitly permit any Friday arrangement for this single party of nine, and, if so, which experience, party minimums and prices would apply?
4. How many guests will not drink, what would their exact charge be for the chosen experience, and is an appointment actually available?

content.text:
## Flowers for nine adults — Friday, November 6

**All three experiences have published Friday offerings, but none is confirmed for your party or date.** Nine adults exceeds Flowers’ six-person threshold for standard reservations, so the group needs an inquiry rather than an assumption of online availability. The year is unspecified; **November 6, 2026 is a Friday**.

Flowers’ [official visit page](https://www.flowerswinery.com/visit-flowers-healdsburg-2-2/) lists:

| Experience | Published price | Duration | Published schedule | What distinguishes it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sonoma Coast Journey** | **$75 per person, non-members**; member benefits apply | **60 minutes** | **Thursday–Monday**; no specific start times published in the cited listing | Three Appellation wines—Pinot Noir and Chardonnay—with a seasonal crudité and snack board, in the gardens or interior spaces. |
| **Estate Vineyard Immersion** | **$130 per person, non-members**; member benefits apply | **90 minutes** | **Thursday–Monday**; no specific start times published in the cited listing | Four estate wines from Camp Meeting Ridge and Sea View Ridge, with elevated food-pairing bites, hosted in a private garden or interior space. |
| **Elements of Site** | **$150 per person, members and non-members**; member discounts apply | **90 minutes** | **10 a.m. Thursday and Friday, or by special request** | Five estate wines, including library-vintage Almar Chardonnay and Cielo & Pietra Pinot Noir Site Series bottlings, with a deeper focus on geology, topography and organic ecosystems. |

### What this means for your group

- **Sonoma Coast Journey** is the lowest-priced and shortest published option.
- **Estate Vineyard Immersion** offers a longer, estate-focused tasting with food pairings and a published private-space format. That description **does not establish accommodation for nine**.
- **Elements of Site** is the most specialized option and the only one with a specific published Friday start: **10 a.m.** A different time is **request-only**, not confirmed availability.

**Group rule:** Advance reservations are required for every experience. Flowers explicitly directs **groups larger than six** and same-day requests to **reservations@flowerswinery.com** or **707.723.4800** under Sonoma Coast Journey and Estate Vineyard Immersion. Elements of Site separately provides those contacts for custom reservation times; its listing does not establish a nine-person capacity. Neither a group inquiry nor a special request guarantees acceptance. [Official policies and experience details](https://www.flowerswinery.com/visit-flowers-healdsburg-2-2/)

**Location:** The visitor venue is **House of Flowers, 4035 Westside Road, Healdsburg, CA 95448**. These are tasting experiences about coastal vineyards—not published tours at Camp Meeting Ridge or Sea View Ridge. The address is corroborated by the [public winery listing](https://www.discoverwine.online/wineries/flowers-winery/).

The prices above are **published reference prices, not a nine-person booking quote**; current inventory, group-specific terms and any applicable extras remain unverified.

**Most useful unresolved questions:** Is the intended year 2026? Can Flowers accommodate all nine together in each experience on that date, and at what times? Would member benefits apply to any guests, and what would the complete group price and cancellation terms be? If Elements of Site at 10 a.m. is unsuitable, would Flowers accept a custom-time request for nine?

North Bay Shuttle advertises private, direct, door-to-door charter transportation serving **OAK and Sonoma**. Its main [price table](https://northbayshuttle.net/price-table/) labels pricing as applying to/from **SFO/OAK**, so these are not substituted SFO-only rates:

| 5–6 people | $280 |

The table also lists **2:00 hours** as a route reference, not a flight-specific travel-time guarantee, and a **$5 credit/debit-card surcharge**.

**Seven-person fit:** Its [Sonoma service page](https://northbayshuttle.net/book-sonoma-county-shuttle-transportation/) says its vans accommodate parties of **up to nine people**. That supports seven passengers in principle; it does **not** establish room for seven adults’ luggage. No vehicle model or luggage capacity is specified in the retrieved evidence.

**Price qualification:** The published tiers stop at six. **$280 is not a seven-person fare**, and no extra-passenger amount is established. A second official [“Price table Editable” page](https://northbayshuttle.net/price-table-editable/) lists conflicting, lower Sonoma rates—$130/$160/$190 for the same passenger bands. The main price page carries a fuel-cost adjustment notice; the lower alternate table should not be treated as the applicable fare without clarification.

**Unresolved:** Seven-person total, exact-hotel applicability, vehicle and baggage capacity, and whether gratuity, airport charges, tolls, waiting time or late-hour charges are included or additional. The retrieved evidence does not establish these amounts.

### 2. Wine Country Airporter — stronger published vehicle-fit evidence, no route rate

[Wine Country Airporter](https://winecountryairporter.com/) advertises **private OAK transfers to Sonoma**, including door-to-door hotel service. Its **12-passenger Executive Sprinter** is described as keeping small groups together with dedicated space planned for baggage.

**Seven-person fit:** This is a supported candidate for seven adults plus luggage, but the exact bag count and sizes still need to fit the assigned vehicle. Its sedan is expressly limited to **1–3 travelers** and is unsuitable; the SUV has no published passenger capacity in the retrieved evidence, so seven-person suitability cannot be assumed.

**Price and fees:** No OAK–Sonoma reference rate appears in the retrieved official evidence. The supplier says quotes depend on route, time, vehicle, passenger count, luggage, direction and meet-and-greet/group requirements. Curbside versus meet-and-greet arrangements, waiting charges and other inclusions remain unpriced.

### Bottom line

**North Bay Shuttle offers the clearest published OAK–Sonoma price reference, but neither a seven-person fare nor confirmed luggage fit. Wine Country Airporter offers clearer group-vehicle evidence, but no published route price.** Neither is an available or confirmed quote for November 5.

The most useful unresolved questions are:

- What is the all-in price for **seven adults, that luggage, and The Lodge at Sonoma**, and which vehicle is included?

content.text:
For **nine guests traveling from the Lodge at Sonoma to Napa wineries and back**, a **vehicle supplied with a professional driver** is the better-supported starting option. **Renting a van and separately hiring a designated driver** is also supported in principle, but requires additional capacity, rental-permission and insurance checks. Neither is a confirmed booking or quote.

### 1. Hire the vehicle and driver together

**SF City Limo** publishes these relevant Sonoma wine-tour vehicles:

| Vehicle | Published passenger fit | Published hourly rate | Seven-hour arithmetic reference* |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Coach-style Mercedes Sprinter | 8–13 passengers; the specific vehicle must accommodate nine guests | $160–$210 | $1,120–$1,470 |
| Limo-style Sprinter | 14 passengers | $210–$260 | $1,470–$1,820 |

Its Sonoma tour page states a **seven-hour minimum**, unlimited mileage and stops, and **additional bridge toll charges**. Crucially, its published rates are for **San Francisco/SFO pickup**; pickup in another city can have a different hourly rate or a travel-time charge. The page explicitly labels some smaller-vehicle rates as gratuity-inclusive, but the retrieved Sprinter listings do **not** establish that gratuity is included. [SF City Limo’s official Sonoma tour page](https://sfcitylimo.com/tours/sonoma/)

\*These multiplications are reference amounts—not Lodge at Sonoma quotes. The actual vehicle assignment, Sonoma pickup pricing, billable travel time, gratuity treatment and other applicable charges remain unknown. A bridge toll should not be assumed necessary without the route.

**Assessment:** Both advertised Sprinter categories offer a plausible nine-guest solution, subject to confirming the actual vehicle’s passenger capacity. The seven-hour minimum is a billing requirement, not evidence that seven hours suits the eventual Napa itinerary.

### 2. Rent a suitable van and hire a designated driver separately

This strategy uses **your rental vehicle**, not a vehicle supplied by the driver service.

- **DD North Bay:** Advertises licensed, insured drivers for vehicles up to 15 passengers. Its published rate for **van rentals or groups of seven or more is $75/hour before gratuity**, with a **six-hour daily minimum**: **$450 minimum driver charge**, before gratuity and rental expenses. It says it can transport only as many people as the vehicle can legally seat. [Official service and pricing](https://ddnorthbay.com/)
- **Simply Driven Napa Sonoma:** Publishes **$60/hour with a five-hour daily minimum**, or **$300 minimum driver charge**. It says its drivers can drive 15-passenger vans and capacity is limited by seatbelts. Gratuity is discretionary; it lists a **$50 deposit to secure the driver**, optional itinerary planning **from $150**, and additional fees for named remote pickup areas. The retrieved terms do not establish a Lodge at Sonoma surcharge or a nine-person surcharge. [Official designated-driver page](https://simplydrivennapasonoma.com/napa-sonoma-designated-driver/)

For nine guests, the rental must legally seat **at least ten people including the hired driver**. No specific rental vehicle, availability, rental rate, taxes, fuel cost, mileage allowance, additional-driver charge or insurance arrangement has been established. The rental agreement must permit the hired driver to operate that vehicle; a driver service’s insurance statement alone does not settle rental authorization or coverage.

**Assessment:** This can work without a sober member of the party, because the designated driver is hired separately. However, the driver-only minimums are **not comparable all-in prices** against SF City Limo’s vehicle-and-driver rates. A rental driven by a member of the group is **not currently a supported plan**, since no willing sober driver is confirmed.

### Most useful unresolved questions

- What date, pickup/return window and Napa winery stops are intended?
- Which exact vehicle will provide nine guest seats plus the driver?
- What is SF City Limo’s Lodge at Sonoma rate, including billable travel time, gratuity and all applicable fees?
- For the rental strategy, what is the complete van cost, and does the rental company authorize and insure the separately hired driver?

Published capacities and prices establish possible options—not current inventory, an accepted itinerary or a booking quote.
